notesStmt.note: Whitman contemplated writing an essay about Elias Hicks for many years. While finishing preparations for the printing of November Boughs, Whitman told Horace Traubel, "Some of these bits were written as many as thirty years ago. Some of them I have written within the past year. They are a miscellaneous lot but they all belong in the same stream" (see Traubel, With Walt Whitman in Camden, 2:42). It is therefore difficult to determine the exact date of the present manuscript. The number printed at the top, "177" was probably added as Whitman worked to organize the various notes and draft material into a coherent essay.
This manuscript is a fragment of a late draft, possibly the the printer's copy, of Whitman's essay "Elias Hicks, Notes (such as they are)," which was first published in November Boughs (1888).

body.p: consent of all the other sects, as the Jews were, ‸in Europe in the middle ages.—In New England, the cruelest laws were passed, and put in execution against them.—‸As said, Some were whipt—women the same as men.—Some had their ears and noses cut off—others their tongues pierced with hot irons.—others ‸their faces branded.—Worse still, a woman and three men were had been hanged, (1660.)—Public opinion, and the statutes, joined together, in an odious union, Quakers, Baptists, ‸Roman Catholics and Witches.—Such a fragmentary sketch of George Fox and his time—and the advent of 'the Society of Friends' in America.
